title: TE Robert C. Peterson, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension
disposition_detail: Specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation sustained; recommendations for remedial action adopted. No separate dismissal or express ruling on the Presbytery's BCO 41 reference is recorded in the source.
first_summary: Ascension Presbytery refused to comply with the Eleventh General Assembly's order to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens's ordination trial and referred the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly under BCO 41 for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted remedial recommendations. It held that BCO 41 cannot be used to refer a prior General Assembly decision back for retrial.
summary: Complaint challenged Ascension Presbytery's March 10, 1984 refusal to obey the Eleventh General Assembly's directive to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens's ordination trial, and its purported BCO 41 reference of the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted recommendations for remedial action. The complaint's asserted distinction—that BCO 41 cannot return a prior General Assembly decision for retrial—marks the case's practical limit.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–3 identify the matter as 12-83, Case 5, before the Committee on Judicial Business at the 12th (1984) General Assembly; line 13 gives the complaint title.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 15–29 describe the complaint against Ascension Presbytery's March 10, 1984 resolution to take no further action on the 11th GA directives and its BCO 41 reference to the 12th GA requesting retrial.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Line 3 supplies the adopted disposition: specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation sustained, and recommendations for remedial action adopted. Lines 21–27 state the complaint's constitutional/BCO grounds; the source does not separately reproduce the full adopted reasoning.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The body text is the Peterson complaint, not a separate opinion. It distinguishes the prior 11th GA decision from a still-open 'case' and alleges BCO 41 is not for referring past GA actions back for retrial.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 15–17 incorporate the 11th GA result: the Barleman complaint was sustained in three of five specifications, and Recommendation #4 directed Ascension Presbytery to correct aspects of the trial contrary to PCA constitutional standards.

source_limits: The source preserves the complaint and a header disposition; it does not reproduce the full CJB/GA opinion, the exact remedial recommendations, or any separate ruling on the BCO 41 reference. The prior 11th GA decision is supplied only in summary form.
